title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 220 (Agent not entitled to remuneration for business misconducted)

content.overview: An agent who is guilty of misconduct in the business of the agency is not entitled to any remuneration in respect of that part of the business which he has misconducted.
content.glance: Misconduct in agency business → no remuneration for the misconducted part.
content.study: An agent who is guilty of misconduct in the business of the agency is not entitled to any remuneration in respect of that part of the business which he has misconducted. Illustration: A employs B to recover 1,000 rupees from C; through B’s misconduct the money is not recovered; B is entitled to no remuneration and must make good the loss.

sections.heading: Misconduct in business of the agency
sections.body: Agent is guilty of misconduct in the business of the agency.

sections.heading: No remuneration for that part
sections.body: No remuneration in respect of the misconducted part of the business.

provisions.title: Agent not entitled to remuneration for business misconducted

examples.title: Statutory illustration
examples.body: A employs B to recover 1,000 rupees from C. Through B’s misconduct the money is not recovered. B is entitled to no remuneration for his services, and must make good the loss.

hypotheticals.question: Do the facts engage Section 220?
hypotheticals.analysis: Compare the facts with the statutory elements in Section 220. If they match, the statutory consequence follows; otherwise it does not.

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 220
distinctions.body: Section 220 applies only to the circumstances described in its statutory text. It does not create additional grounds or remedies beyond those stated.

misconceptions.myth: Section 220 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
misconceptions.correction: Section 220 operates only within the elements and consequences stated in its statutory text.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 220 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify misconduct; deny remuneration for that part; address loss if pleaded.

illustrations.body: A employs B to recover 1,000 rupees from C. Through B’s misconduct the money is not recovered. B is entitled to no remuneration for his services, and must make good the loss.
